LESSON: FICTION AND NON- FICTION 8.3.2: NON- FICTION PROSE: LITERARY/ NARRATIVE JOURNALISM

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: LITERATURE IN ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.3: Fiction and Non- Fiction 8.3.2: Non- fiction prose: Literary/ narrative Journalism
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Fiction and Non- Fiction 8.3.2: Non- fiction prose: Literary/ narrative Journalism, part of Strand 8 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 LITERATURE IN ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How can literary journalism promote lifelong learning?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. describe literary journalism for literary appreciation,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Fiction and Non- Fiction 8.3.2: Non- fiction prose: Literary/ narrative Journalism in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. discuss form and features in literary journalism for literary analysis,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Fiction and Non- Fiction 8.3.2: Non- fiction prose: Literary/ narrative Journalism in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. analyse the subject matter of literary journalism for literary appreciation,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Fiction and Non- Fiction 8.3.2: Non- fiction prose: Literary/ narrative Journalism in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the importance

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Fiction and Non- Fiction 8.3.2: Non- fiction prose: Literary/ narrative Journalism in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read a story from a magazine or newspaper. Learners with speech difficulties could be given more considerable time,
2. brainstorm on the meaning of literary journalism,
3. search online or offline for form and features of literary journalism and present their findings in

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Fiction and Non- Fiction 8.3.2: Non- fiction prose: Literary/ narrative Journalism together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: This is enhanced as the learner carries out research to find information to write stories based on a true

account.

● Digital literacy: This is developed when the learner interacts with technology when searching online or offline for form and

features of literary journalism and presents their findings in class.

Values:
Responsibility: This is achieved when the learner exhibits self-discipline when seeking information from online and offline

sources to write stories based on a true account.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Citizenship: This is enhanced as the learner collaborates to identify the form and features of literary journalism.
